content:
Laredo College has a new trustee, and no voter had a say in picking him. At a special called meeting on October 12, the college's Board of Trustees voted unanimously to appoint Luis F. Mendoza III to Board Position 3, the seat left open when longtime Trustee Mercurio Martinez Jr. retired on September 24, according to the college.

Mendoza holds a Bachelor of Business Administration in Entrepreneurship from St. Edward's University and works in finance — the college says his background includes work as a licensed financial advisor and in anti-money laundering investigations, along with experience analyzing complex financial information. All seven trustees in attendance voted in favor of the appointment.

Fifteen people applied for the seat during a fourteen-day public call for applications, and the college says trustees reviewed the applicants using a scoring rubric built from the eligibility and ethics requirements in board policy.

Why there was no election

The college says appointment was the only legal route available. Martinez retired on September 24 — after the filing deadline for the November 3, 2026 election had already passed — so the seat could not be placed on this fall's ballot, and a new board policy adopted in August (BBC LOCAL) required the vacancy to be filled by the next regular board election date. The college also notes this is familiar ground: its past two trustee vacancies were filled by appointment as well, making this the third consecutive time a seat on the board that governs Laredo College has been filled by the trustees themselves rather than by the public.

Mendoza will serve the remainder of Martinez's unexpired term, after which the seat returns to the regular election cycle and voters decide who holds it.

What to watch

An appointed trustee votes on the same budgets, contracts, tax matters and presidential oversight as an elected one. Mendoza's finance and anti-money laundering background will now be part of the board's fiduciary oversight of a public college — and Webb Watch will be watching how the board's newest member votes, starting with the college's next meetings.

Sources: Laredo College, "LC board appoints new trustee to fill Position 3 vacancy," laredo.edu, Oct. 19, 2026; Laredo College, "Laredo College seeks applicants to fill Board of Trustees vacancy," laredo.edu, Sept. 25, 2026.

title: A New Laredo College Trustee Takes His Seat by Appointment, Not Election
